how_customers_find_and_choose: Vehicle owners find workshops, washes and parts shops through the map listing, reviews and recommendations from other owners
Buyers of vehicles search online listings with photos and short videos and ask for details in chat before visiting
Customers judge honesty by whether a workshop explains the fault, shows the old part and gives a clear written estimate
Business customers for fleets, buses and rentals choose on reliability, availability and clear contracts
Aviation customers and operators are reached through trade contacts and regulated channels, not mass marketing
what_works_now: A written job card or estimate with the fault found, parts and agreed work, sent in chat before work starts
Photos or a short video of the problem sent to the owner during the repair
A service reminder to customers when the next oil, tyre or battery check is due, with consent
Honest listings for used vehicles with real photos, condition notes and a short walkaround video
A complete map listing with hours, services and a pin that is easy to find
Asking customers for a review after a job done well
Tracking repeat visits and common faults by vehicle type to plan stock and staff
outdated_or_weak: Quoting by phone without seeing the vehicle and then changing the price
Hiding the old parts or doing work without approval
Listings with copied photos or hidden defects
Printed handbills at petrol pumps as the main source of customers
Free-wash or discount stunts that bring one-time customers

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Fuel price changes, heat and monsoon flooding affect vehicle demand and workshop load
Vehicle imports and registration are regulated; the owner confirms specifics with the authority
Many repairs are paid in cash on completion
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Vehicle ownership and rental are high; summer heat makes cooling, tyres and batteries common jobs
Transport and aviation businesses are licensed by their authority; the owner confirms specifics
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Winter driving drives tyre changes and battery checks; seasonal demand is strong
Auto repair and sales are consumer-protected by province; the owner confirms specifics

never_assume: A digital job card or service history
A video or photo process on the shop floor
